correctness.rationale: The four maps exhaust all complete two-state tables with the stated acceptance convention. An O-letter repeated n times allows all shorter prefixes, giving mex n, the upper bound from at most n options. With no O or T the accepting state is never reached. With swaps but no resets an accepted suffix toggles parity; odd positions have the empty option and even positions have no zero-valued option, proving the pointwise parity rule. In the remaining case, if the last block has even parity, accepted suffixes lie within that block and leave positive-valued prefixes by induction. If it has odd parity, cuts before the last reset are all allowed; the first T in each earlier T-bearing block realizes the next positive integer, and cuts within the final block leave zero. This yields precisely the mex equal to the number of T-bearing blocks. A value k needs k swaps and k−1 separators, and T(ZT)^(k−1) and ZT(ZT)^(k−1) give equality for both length parities. Renaming letters by transition type preserves all legal cuts and the mex induction, but arbitrary codeword recodings need not.
residual_risks: The checker word counts are consistent with 64·Σ_{n=1}^8 3^n and 16·Σ_{n=1}^{16} 2^n. The finite regressions cannot establish all lengths or alphabets; that is the role of the induction.

The coset result counts prefix visits in a group action, where all letters are invertible. A reset is noninvertible; more concretely in a finite group some positive power of a letter reaches the identity subgroup, whereas no positive power of a rejecting reset is accepted in the mixed case.
The two-sided binary and balanced-suffix results use different move cuts.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Relabeling letters by their four types is an exact reduction for this problem. Neither a group/subgroup monoid nor a rule allowing prefix deletions or length-balance constraints is an equivalent encoding of the mixed reset/swap game.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: An even-length coincidence of floor(n/2) with ceil(n/2) is not an exact table match for the same game, and finite enumeration does not determine the maxima at arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: The supported contribution is the complete all-length maximum law and, especially, the pointwise mixed reset/swap formula. Fixed-value regularity, elementary parity and the mex recurrence are antecedents or standard ingredients. The closest sources give general language regularity, or exact laws for different deletion rules; no checked stronger result covers the reset/swap classification.
residual_risks: The passage and catalogue searches were bounded. Unindexed equivalent classifications are not excluded; no same-day priority is inferred.

value.rationale: This completely resolves the first nontrivial DFA-state class for a natural boundedness question. The growing case without an accepting reset is not explained by the obvious unary accepting-reset strategy: intervening rejecting resets create many distinct mex levels. Both the sharp growth constant and the individual formula are useful beyond deciding which tables are bounded.
residual_risks: No result here for larger automata, other deletion conventions, or all pointwise values in the O-letter regime.
